Freddie Potts on the pain of leaving West Ham, why he had to move on this summer, upsetting the odds in the Champions League with Club Brugge - and why they don't fear Liverpool!

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1303 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.
  • Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

Industry observers note that ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts claims. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the aims as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

According to recent reports, potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

It has been revealed that in Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

He is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

In a recent development, ‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he indicates. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a latest language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

Sources indicate that potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his latest surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts states. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

According to recent reports, potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

Sources indicate that ‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

Industry observers note that ‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

Industry observers note that ‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

It has been revealed that “I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old noted. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he remarked. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

Sources indicate that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he stated. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

It has been revealed that for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

Industry observers note that “The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage stated. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

With less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

"Would you look at that!" DIEGO GOMEZ SCORES FROM THE HALFWAY LINE! 🤯 https://t.co/qmagVbGEb4.

“I’m not training with Diego Gómez shooting from 50 metres in training,” head coach Fabian Hürzeler said while breaking into a smile. “It’s just about making the players quick in their minds.

Sources indicate that “In these moments it’s about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and being quick to go to the action was impressive.”.

The presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. As he looked up to confirm the opportunity, the 23-year-old struck the ball over Benítez with such venom that it did not even bounce until it reached the goal.

All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Recent findings suggest that gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

Gómez may well attempt an encore. He shot from even further out at the Stadium of Light a week ago. When October ends, three of the last four Premier League goal-of-the-month winners will be Brighton players. Alongside his meticulous emphasis on set-pieces, Hürzeler empowers flair in open play.

In a recent development, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

According to recent reports, brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Recent findings suggest that yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German stated: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

Sources indicate that in his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Industry observers note that elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

From there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It has been revealed that it was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

It has been revealed that ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

It has been revealed that milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Sources indicate that rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

It has been revealed that frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

It has been revealed that out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

According to recent reports, milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Sources indicate that frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

Industry observers note that the second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Sources indicate that ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

Sources indicate that frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine rapidly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Industry observers note that frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

It has been revealed that ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

Sources indicate that after the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

The Lilywhites have returned to the top half of the Premier League table as a result, and De Zerbi now seeks a slice of revenge after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Sunderland in his Tottenham debut last season.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Tottenham's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their meeting with the Black Cats, who are 18th in the rankings with nine points from 11 games.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Sandro Tonali was absent from last Saturday's win over Ipswich due to illness, but he has returned to Tottenham training and is expected to be available for the weekend.

Savio returned from a muscular injury as a second-half substitute against Ipswich, but the Brazilian attacker then had to come off with a similar matter towards the end.

The severity of Savio's latest concern is not clear, but there is little to no chance of him facing Sunderland.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Tosin Adarabioyo had made a full recovery from a calf injury before last weekend's triumph, but he was not risked by De Zerbi.

However, if the defender can prove his fitness this week, he should be in the matchday squad at the Stadium of Light.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

Chelsea loanee Mykhaylo Mudryk is still on the mend from an ankle injury, and the Ukrainian is not expected to return to action for another couple of weeks.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: February 20 (vs. Brighton & Hove Albion).

Xavi Simons is almost seven months into his recovery from an ACL rupture, and all being well, the Dutchman could make his comeback in mid to late February.

Possible return date: February 6 (vs. Ipswich Town).

Likewise, Wilson Odobert will not play again in 2026 due to his own serious knee injury, but De Zerbi is hopeful that the winger will return to full training in January ahead of a potential February return.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

De Zerbi revealed last week that Mathys Tel will need another "two or three weeks" to recover from the ankle injury he picked up against Leeds, so the Frenchman could be targeting a comeback for the North London derby on December 6.

Tottenham have no players banned for this game.

Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

It has been revealed that morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS noted: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

According to recent reports, A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s new biology skills wow scientists

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.
  • Earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins.
  • He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

Earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology firm called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary newly introduced proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed upcoming proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

It has been revealed that the research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” states Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

Sources indicate that but some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

In a recent development, the release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 introduced a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing newly introduced proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, claims Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

Sources indicate that in other experiments, the OpenAI team highlighted that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

Industry observers note that jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03836-z.

Sources indicate that the high was Jordan Young’s double clinching Saturday’s 2-1 Woodside Road win over second-placed Harrogate. The low was letting in three in four minutes to scupper their hopes of a result at Woking on Tuesday night.

Boss Adam Hinshelwood was as frustrated in midweek as he had been pleased at the weekend – and is demanding more consistency from his players, particularly in their defending.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After Saturday’s win, Hinshelwood mentioned the display showed his squad were learning as they went.

Industry observers note that he mentioned: “It was probably one of our best wins if you look at where Harrogate are in the league and that we’d come off the back of that late goal conceded at Scunthorpe the previous week. We wanted a response to that and got it.

“They probably shaded the first half but we scored at a good time – in fact Jordan scored twice at good times.

“At 1-1 we had a real go and demonstrates how far we have come. Settling for a draw just isn’t in our mindset. We’ve had a few games that could have gone either way but we will always try to win games.

“The second goal came from the type of move we’ve been working on in training.”.

It has been revealed that hinshelwood is delighted by Young’s influence on the campaign. He signed from Torquay in September after Teddy Jenks left the Reds – and he’s proved the perfect replacement so far.

It has been revealed that “He’s a top talent who we’d chased for a while. He’d done it against us too many times and we knew what he could do for us.”.

Young has scored six goals in 15 appearances and Hinshelwood said: “He is scoring, assisting and creating.”.

But Tuesday’s loss at Woking – where goals by Ashley Nathaniel-George and Dominic Johnson-Fisher (2) proved in vain – left Hinshelwood hugely frustrated.

Sources indicate that “We’re gifting games to our opponents. They don’t have to do anything to beat us. We scored two unbelievable goals but gifted them goals – and it’s a common trend,” he told club media.

“Good teams are consistent week after week but we have turned up and just thought we can do enough to win. At this level you get found out.

It has been revealed that “We have no-one to blame but ourselves. Three goals in four minutes – it’s nowhere near good enough. We’ve got to find a way to defend our box on a consistent basis.”.

The seventh-placed Rebels go to Altrincham on Saturday then visit Wick next Tuesday in the Sussex Senior Cup third round.

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1350 w)

The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs new lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

It has been revealed that williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

According to recent reports, this is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a new contract at the club.

According to recent reports, he said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

It has been revealed that 'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'.

Recent findings suggest that hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

Recent findings suggest that he does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

Industry observers note that his brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Recent findings suggest that here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

Recent findings suggest that the Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Recent findings suggest that spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

Industry observers note that it is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping concerns but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

It has been revealed that although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' stated De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'.

Hollands’ men go into the keenly anticipated showdown on the back of a hard-fought 2-1 home win over an in-form Hayes & Yeading United outfit last time out.

Goals from Luke Roberts and Henry McDonald secured the victory and a vital three points that keep the home side in the reckoning at the top end of the standings — and Hollands believes a win is in his side’s grasp at the Springfield Stadium.

Sources indicate that he told the club’s official YouTube channel: “We’ve got to worry about ourselves more so than we do Jersey. We will obviously pay them respect; we're going to their home ground and they're doing well so you have to pay the respect.

“But we must make sure that we have a plan suitable for us to get three points away from home, which will be a tough ask — but it's something that I feel we can achieve if we play to the heights that we have done this season.

“We have to have belief because we have shown that on our day we can compete with some of the best teams in this division.

“I've got belief in them. It's all about what we can do and how we can influence games. I feel if we turn up, then we can compete with anyone, but we have to show that and have to do so on a more consistent basis.”.

The most recent triumph — which came after a home win over Littlehampton Town — further addressed a mini-slump in the league and the gaffer says his charges should take the positives from getting back on track.

He added: “We must take the positives from two league wins on the spin and make sure we go there (Jersey) with the confidence that provides.”.

Pep Guardiola names three former midfielders he expects to become good managers, including an ex-Man City player

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:15.
  • Pep Guardiola believes that midfielders have characteristics that can make the transition from the pitch to the technical area easier.
  • In an interview with Romario TV, the former Manchester City manager spoke about players who, in his view, have the potential to build a successful career as managers, and highlighted the broader vision of the game that the position requires.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:15.

Pep Guardiola believes that midfielders have characteristics that can make the transition from the pitch to the technical area easier.

In an interview with Romario TV, the former Manchester City manager spoke about players who, in his view, have the potential to build a successful career as managers, and highlighted the broader vision of the game that the position requires.

Industry observers note that among the names mentioned are Ilkay Gundogan, Sergio Busquets and Xabi Alonso, all with midfield experience and different trajectories in football. When asked about former players who could follow in his footsteps on the touchline, Guardiola was direct in naming his picks.

Sources indicate that 'I think Gundogan will be a good manager... Busquets will be a good manager. I knew Xabi Alonso would become a good manager.'.

The statement brings together three players who played notable roles in elite teams and who, during their careers, played in roles that demanded game reading, tactical understanding and the ability to organise collective actions.

The choice of names follows the central idea presented by the manager. For Guardiola, experience as a midfielder can offer an especially favourable base for those who want to lead a team. That is because the position requires involvement at different moments of the match, in both attacking build-up and defensive organisation, as well as a constant understanding of the positioning of team-mates and opponents.

Recent findings suggest that guardiola explained why he sees an advantage in players who operate in that area. In the Catalan's view, the role demands a reading that goes beyond individual participation, as the midfielder needs to understand how the team moves and what each moment of the match requires.

'I think midfielders have an advantage because they need to have a more global understanding of the game' - he mentioned.

It has been revealed that the manager deepened his reasoning by drawing a comparison with forwards. 'They have to make the team play and understand which areas to defend. A forward often just thinks: "I am going to score a goal, and that is it."'.

The observation is not a criticism of forwards, but highlights the difference in responsibilities between the positions.

While a forward can concentrate much of his performance on finishing and the pursuit of goals, the midfielder needs to follow the collective dynamic, identify spaces, take part in ball circulation and understand the movements required to protect the team without possession.

Industry observers note that the three names cited by the manager have trajectories that help explain his assessment. Gundogan worked with Guardiola at Manchester City, while Busquets was a key part of Barcelona during the period when Guardiola managed the team. Xabi Alonso, meanwhile, was coached by Guardiola at Bayern Munich.

What they have in common, beyond the position, is that all three built careers marked by the ability to interpret the game and make decisions in different tactical contexts.

In a recent development, in Alonso's case, Guardiola had already shown this perception before the former midfielder began his managerial career. The Spaniard retired as a player in 2017 and later rose to prominence in charge of Bayer Leverkusen, work that reinforced the bet made by his former manager.

Gundogan and Busquets are also examples of players who, through the experience accumulated in elite football, inspire Guardiola's confidence when it comes to a possible career in management.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

City drew 2-2 with Basingstoke Town last Saturday – and the two goals they conceded came when they were playing against ten men.

That was after Kristian Shevchenko – son of one-time Ballon D’or winner Andriy – was sent off in the first half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Chi coach Darin Killpartrick credited Basingstoke with making it difficult for his team by changing shape when they went down to ten men.

But he said he was disappointed by the way City defended for the two they let in – and it had to be viewed as an opportunity for three points passed up.

Chi are back at Oaklands Park this Saturday and it’s leaders Uxbridge who are the visitors.

It has been revealed that uxbridge handed City their biggest defeat of the season to date at home in mid-September – it finished 5-0 in Middlesex. And Killpartrick has warned Chi will need to be at their very best to try to get anything out of the game.

Will Sweet and Emmett Dunn were the scorers against Basingstoke as City led 1-0 and 2-1.

Killpartrick noted: “It was a missed opportunity for the win against a team who ended with ten men; however when they went down to ten, they changed to a shape that was very difficult to break down.

“We cannot defend – as a team – like we did for their two goals.

It has been revealed that “Their first goal upset me the most. Their player has weaved around four or five players and from us that’s not the level we need to produce.

“If you defend like that at this level of football, you will get punished – particularly if you are playing top teams like that.

“But we’ve had a look at it and talked it through with the players and they know we need to defend better than that.”.

One major relief for City is that their long run of Tuesday night matches is over, at least for now.

Killpartrick said the relentless schedule since September had stretched their small squad to the limit and it was great to have a Tuesday when they could concentrate on training, and having a bit of fun as a group too.

According to recent reports, another boost is that two key players – midfielder Lloyd Rowlatt and defender Curtis Da Costa – are fit again and pushing for spots. James Sweet has trained again after a hamstring injury.

A big crowd is hoped for on Saturday, Killpartrick saying: “You’ll see two good teams trying to play entertaining football – we hope for plenty of support.”.

Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.
  • An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Industry observers note that but United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

Industry observers note that ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving swiftly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ mentioned Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

Sources indicate that ‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a newly introduced contact stalled.

It has been revealed that ‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

According to recent reports, asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.
  • For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.
  • Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

Industry observers note that “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He noted that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Recent findings suggest that sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

Sources indicate that the mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, claims Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

According to recent reports, shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, remarked Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts right now on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

Sources indicate that ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 09:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 09:29.

Anthony Gordon scored twice in Barcelona's 4-1 win over Sabah in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

In doing so, Gordon made history - the forward has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the England international's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice against Sabah on Wednesday.

Lamine Yamal missed out through injury, while Raphinha was rested from the start, with Gordon joined by Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus in the final third, and all three found the back of the net.

As expected, Gordon's performance brought a lot of praise from the Spanish media.

6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch.

AS were extremely positive about Gordon's performance, saying that the forward was 'vital' to Barcelona securing all three points in the Champions League.

Mundo Deportivo also highlighted how well he combined with Gabriel Jesus and Adeyemi in the final third of the field in the absence of Yamal and Raphinha.

La Vanguardia concentrated on how Gordon became the main player in the Barcelona attack and remarked that he was one of the main reasons why Hansi Flick's side were able to score four goals.

Culemania said that Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes', having netted twice in the absence of the Brazil international, who has scored 19 times in all competitions this season.

Gordon will never be the main man in the Barcelona attack due to the presence of both Yamal and Raphinha, but he has played an vital supporting role this term.

The 25-year-old's numbers for this season are relatively solid, coming up with five goals and five assists in 17 appearances in all competitions.

In La Liga, Gordon has two goals and five assists in 12 appearances, while he has struck three times in five outings in the Champions League.

The forward will be looking to improve his goal total in Spain's top flight, but it has been a positive start to his Barcelona career for the former Everton youngster.

Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet.
  • In the end it also points to another thing.
  • Recent findings suggest that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

Recent findings suggest that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

According to recent reports, “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

It has been revealed that defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

Recent findings suggest that that is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

Recent findings suggest that we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and noted he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Sources indicate that with all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

Recent findings suggest that this has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After Ashley Nathaniel-George cancelled out Roy Syla’s opener just before half-time, a five minute spree including two goals from John Marquis and an own-goal from Harvey Griffiths turned the tide heavily in favour of the hosts after the interval.

Dominic Johnson-Fisher’s superb showing from the bench brought the Rebels within touching distance of leaving Surrey with a point after the number nine netted twice, but the deficit could not be overturned before the full-time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Recent findings suggest that it was the hosts who enjoyed the better start of the two side through 20 minutes, as experienced forward Marquis had two sights on goal early on. A driving run down the right flank by Jaiden Putman inside the first minute led to the former Portsmouth striker being picked out at the far post, yet he could not get an effort away under pressure from multiple Worthing bodies.

Five minutes later, another breakaway for the Cardinals saw Marquis latch onto a lofted ball in behind the Rebels backline. Shaping onto his left side, the 34 year-old’s strike was kept out by the midriff of Harrison Foulkes.

Worthing had spells of promise during the early exchanges, with the weekend’s match-winner Jordan Young instrumental once again in most of the away side’s attacking play. The former Torquay United man had his best effort of the half just after quarter of an hour, linking up with Kendall through the right channel before firing over Vicente Reyes’ crossbar.

According to recent reports, putman’s adventurous play down the Woking right posed a persistent threat to the left of the visitors’ defence throughout the first half. The QPR-loanee tested Foulkes with an attempt of his own with 20 minutes on the clock drifting inward from the right side before being kept out by another Foulkes intervention.

With half an hour on the clock, a double substitution from Hinshelwood to bring on both Cory Adjetey-Brew and Nathaniel-George proved the spark for a crescendo of action to close out the half.

A loose ball following an aerial challenge allowed Putman to drive forward down the right. The ball found the feet of Josh Kelly at the by-line, who swivelled before picking out the run of Syla into the box. With Syla unmarked, the midfielder side-footed the ball past Foulkes to open the scoring.

Woking’s first half advantage did not last long, and it was one of the two first half changes in Nathaniel-George who fashioned an equaliser with a minute of normal time remaining in the period. Cutting in from the left flank, the substitute curled a right-footed strike which nestled into Reyes’ bottom left corner from 20 yards out. A spectacular way to open his goalscoring account for the Rebels.

While Worthing’s rapid response may have spurned optimism amongst the travelling faithful heading into the break, the start of the second half spelled nothing but turmoil from a Worthing perspective.

Less than a minute after play resumed, Marquis notched his second of the night after turning the ball home from the edge of the six-yard box with a flicked finish amidst a sea of away defenders.

The hosts doubled their advantage almost immediately after regaining their lead. A poorly-executed pass from Foulkes invited Woking to spring an attack, and with the visitors’ keeper stranded off his goal-line, Marquis swept home into an empty net to make it 3-1.

Five minutes of horror to start the half culminated with the home side adding a fourth goal. Another giveaway in midfield presented Josh Grant the opportunity to drive towards the box. Grant’s eventual effort fizzed off the foot of the retreating Griffiths, with Foulkes helpless to watch the ball trickle over the line.

According to recent reports, the away contingent stunned following a flurry of concessions, Hinshelwood looked to the bench yet again for inspiration in giving the Rebels a chance of coming away with something. One of those introductions was Johnson-Fisher, who netted two brilliant goals to bring the visitors back to within one.

In the 64th minute, a ball in from the left side was brought down astutely by the former Whitehawk striker, who fired the ball home on the turn off the underside of the crossbar. Then, 12 minutes later, another fine finish from Johnson-Fisher gave Worthing their third, this time getting on the end of a low pass in behind from Nathaniel-George before slotting a low drive underneath the body of Reyes.

Ultimately, despite the visitors’ best efforts in the closing stages. three goals in rapid succession to start the second half proved too much for the away side to overcome on a cold Tuesday night of madness at the Kingfield Stadium.

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:38.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has reportedly signed a upcoming Leeds United contract running until the summer of 2029.

Daniel Farke's side have continued their excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign following the November international break, recording a 4-1 success at the Stamford Bridge home of Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

As a result of Lukas Nmecha and organization collecting maximum points from the West London contest, the Elland Road club have stayed in seventh position in the Premier League standings, on the coattails of the Champions League conversation.

The main man in attack for Leeds in recent times, Calvert-Lewin has made a positive start to the season, with the 29-year-old Leeds star supposedly wanted by relegation-threatened Manchester United.

Nevertheless, the England international will be fully focused on helping Farke's troops qualify for European competition this term, with the Whites welcoming Coventry City to Yorkshire on Saturday.

According to The Athletic's Beren Cross via transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Leeds United supporters have been given a major piece of positive news regarding the future of leading marksman Calvert-Lewin.

The report claims that the 29-year-old has agreed to an extension of his current terms at Elland Road, with the Three Lions appearance-maker originally joining on a free transfer from Everton in August 2025.

It is understood that Calvert-Lewin's fresh deal will run until the conclusion of the 2028-29 campaign, at which point the striker will be heading towards his mid-30s and the twilight of his career.

Before Leeds can officially announce the news surrounding the forward, it is believed that they must complete 'formal steps', with everyone involved in the process expecting a smooth process in that respect.

Either side of the November international break, Calvert-Lewin's side have recorded back-to-back wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, proving their strength against some of the Premier League's biggest names.

Part of the furniture in the Premier League since the 2017-18 campaign, Calvert-Lewin has been the classic example of a confidence and purple-patch striker, with the attacker's form swinging dramatically.

This season, the 29-year-old is arguably churning out the best performances of his top-flight career to date, scoring five goals and providing one assist during the opening 11 Premier League games.

Whilst Leeds are known to be in the market for another striker ahead of the January window, there is no desire to replace Calvert-Lewin in the starting XI, as is clear with a contract extension on the table.

  • This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.
