📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.

Chris Simmons’ Heath side knew it would be a difficult match up against a Dockers side on top form, second in the division with games in-hand and with the best home record in the division having played eight and won all eight.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was the Bears who had the first shot on target on 9 minutes when Sam Hards was brought down some 30 yards from goal and Ben Royall stepped up to take the resulting free-kick – hitting a left foot shot that was saved comfortably low to his left by the Dockers goalkeeper Javern Pitterson.

On 16 minutes Erith were awarded a free-kick wide on the right and just outside the penalty area, James Dyer played the ball into the danger area where it pinged in and around the 6 yard box before being cleared by Brad Peters and that set the tone for the first half with the hosts having most of the play but unable to break down the solid Bears defence.

Broadbridge Heath did have a few chances, Royall tried to catch Pitterson out with a shot to the near-post but the keeper got back to gather and Ollie Rawlins had a left foot shot saved by Pitterson diving low to his left and it was 0-0 at the break.

The Dockers stepped up a gear in the second half, kicking down the slope, and had the Bears pinned back in their own half for long periods but without really troubling goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield, plenty of goal attempts but everyone charged down by a Broadbridge Heath player defending like their lives depended on it.

On 75 minutes a rare foray deep into the Erith half saw Charlie Connell brought down by a clumsy challenge some 25 yards from goal, Ben Royal stepped up to take the resulting free-kick striking a left foot shot that deflected off the wall wrong-footing Pitterson who could do nothing but watch the ball fly into the net out of his reach.

The hosts continued to push players forward in search of an equaliser but just couldn’t get past the Broadbridge Heath defensive lines who stood firm and dealt with everything the Dockers could throw at them – and it remained 0-1 at the final whistle with Heath continuing their remarkable run of having scored in every league game this season.

Simmons said afterwards: “This one was a bit of a smash and grab, Erith are a very good side and should of gone in front in the first half, defensively we were excellent and our shape and organisation was top notch and in the end got the lucky break the lads deserved.”.

Next up for the Bears is the visit of division leaders Faversham Town to the Air Engineering Stadium on Saturday.

BBH: Hadfield, Cotton, Royall, Marino, Peters, Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Doughty 71), Rawlins, Holden, Hards.

In a recent development, di Paola told us: “I don’t think we played particularly well. I can’t argue with the scoreline. There are no real arguments, really. I think they were the better team.

According to recent reports, “The pitch meant you couldn’t really play any football, but that suited them. I’m not a football snob. There’s no wrong or right way of playing football. The way they play is effective and works for them.

According to recent reports, “It’s not a vanity contest, it’s a winning games contest and they beat us. I’ve no complaints with the result, I just don’t enjoy watching that kind of football.

“I wasn’t that frustrated, angry or disappointed after the game, I just felt we didn’t have the right amount of intensity – and it’s not the kind of place you can go without an intent to battle and fight.”.

Horsham then became the first side to defeat second-placed Truro in National League South since mid-September.

Sources indicate that reece Myles-Meekums’ 16th minute strike proved to be the difference between the two sides. The win leaves the Hornets 14th in the table.

Sources indicate that di Paola added: “If either them or Ebbsfleet don’t win the league then I couldn’t tell you who would. They’re by far and away the best two teams we’ve played.

“We had to suffer but we suffered as a unit. I don’t think Michael [Dike] had loads to do in goal. He made one good save but in general he was sweeping and tidying up.

It has been revealed that “The game would have been made much easier if Nadders [Ashley Nadesan] had scored his one-on-one in the second half. It would have taken the game away from them – but if you don’t score the second you have to suffer.

“That’s something we know we have to do better at, putting teams away. But it’s such a hard league.

“It was always going to be a huge challenge. I don’t think Truro had lost in a couple of months. They’re a top, top side, so to collect a win was really pleasing.”.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, goalkeeper Sam Howes has had his contract cancelled by the Hornets. His departure has seen the return of young Brighton stopper Dike on a 28-day loan.

Horsham travel to sixth-placed Billericay Town this Saturday – and Di Paola revealed a number of his midfielders were stricken going into the the trip to Essex.

He stated: “Everyone’s on their backsides at the moment! Ronan [Silva] is a doubt. He’s been so unlucky. He took a bash to his ankle [against Truro] and it swelled up. It’s not his hamstring, which is one good thing.

“Charlie played injured against Truro because we needed him – but those are the kinds of boys we want at the football club.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:44.

During the 2025 summer transfer window, Liverpool broke the bank, spending £410m.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were the two most expensive signings, as the Swedish striker arrived for £123m (€145m) and the German attacking midfielder for £106m (€125m). But for many months, the two most expensive recruits in the club's history failed to live up to expectations.

In his first season at Liverpool, Wirtz scored seven goals and provided 10 assists in 49 games, but his impact was largely disappointing. Isak, for his part, barely played (four goals and one assist in 22 games) because of a fractured fibula. That summer 2025 transfer window was thus described as 'the worst transfer window in Premier League history'.

Both attackers were therefore expected to deliver in their second season at Liverpool, with latest manager Andoni Iraola arriving.

The momentum is completely different at the start of this campaign, as the 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night in the Champions League illustrated perfectly. Isak scored twice, while Wirtz also found the net.

Industry observers note that the Swede is rediscovering the efficiency that made his reputation at Newcastle United. He now has ten goals in all competitions in 16 games and has just scored in six consecutive away games for Liverpool. The 27-year-old is establishing himself as the number nine Liverpool had long been waiting for.

On Wednesday night, Isak was asked about when he would be back at his best level: 'It is always difficult to say, but I can definitely say that I feel good, the team is in a good rhythm, that is the most notable thing' - he stated.

After a season of adaptation to English football, in which he struggled to have an impact in the final third and to be decisive, Wirtz is in excellent form.

Still deployed as a number 10, the 23-year-old German has scored four goals and provided five assists in 17 games in all competitions for Liverpool.

His November has been excellent: three goals and two assists in three games for Liverpool, as well as three goals in two games for the German national team. Wirtz appears to have digested his huge transfer and to be ready to shed his 'flop' label at Liverpool.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a sport obsessed with the next big thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 25 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next big thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

According to recent reports, of course, injuries, personal concerns and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

It has been revealed that in 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

But things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

Sources indicate that after making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

From that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is at the moment plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

Industry observers note that the first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

Sources indicate that however, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

Sources indicate that but his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

According to recent reports, the Brazilian is currently imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

In a recent development, mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

But the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

Sources indicate that the Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never showed his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the big transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a major-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

The Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

Sources indicate that after six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

It seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

After a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

In a recent development, two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is said and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45.
  • Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.
  • The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45.

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier mentioned than done.

Paris Saint-Germain Ligue 1 form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts.

Lorient possible starting lineup:.

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin.

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

The brain keeps the score: how trauma leaves molecular scars in cells

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.
  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering upcoming insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering upcoming insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, claims Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

Sources indicate that PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

The study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

In a recent development, many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” states study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

According to recent reports, the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

Industry observers note that the researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

Hearts will attempt to claim a major European scalp when they host French giants Monaco in the Uefa Conference League on Thursday evening.

Wouter Vrancken’s side go into the match as underdogs but are in need of a positive result after collecting just one point from their opening three league phase fixtures to sit 32nd in the Conference League table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A 1-1 draw against Norwegian side Nordsjælland at Tynecastle was followed by away defeats at Trabzonspor (2-0) and FC Thun (3-1) to leave the Tynecastle club facing an uphill task to qualify for the knockout stages.

Teams typically need seven or eight points from their six league phase matches to finish inside the top 24 and reach the knockout play-off round. Eight points virtually guarantees progression, while seven points usually puts a club right on the cut-off line where tie-breakers decide who advances.

Hearts know this only too well, having failed to progress on goals scored after collecting seven points to finish 25th during their 2024-25 Conference League campaign.

Monaco arrive in Edinburgh fourth in the table with a maximum haul of nine points following victories over CSKA Sofia, Nordsjælland and Freiburg. Their domestic form has been less impressive of late with Filipe Luís’ side currently on a five-game winless run on Ligue 1, where they are eighth in the standings.

Sources indicate that the Conference League match between Hearts and Monaco takes place at Tynecastle Park, Edinburgh, on Thursday, November 26, 2026. Kick-off is 5.45pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 5pm.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

Hearts welcome midfielder Blair Spittal back into their Europa League squad following his recovery from an ankle injury. Malachi Fagan-Walcott drops out with a groin problem. Two players who featured in the 8-0 win over Dundee on Saturday, Eduardo Ageu and Leart Kabashi, cannot play as they are not registered in the Europa League squad list.

According to recent reports, midfielder Tomas Magnusson is still completing concussion protocol before he can be declared available. Defender Craig Halkett and the versatile Oisin McEntee were back on the Riccarton training pitch on Wednesday, although they will not be back until next month. Winger Calvin Miller has also undergone surgery on his knee and will be out for between six weeks and two months.

Stephen Kingsley (hamstring), Harry Milne (knee) and Tom Renaud (ankle) are also unavailable.

Monaco are without five players. Goalkeeper Philippe Kohn, defender Mohammed Salisu, midfielders Stanis Idumbo and Aleksandr Golovin, plus forward Paris Brunner were all left in the Principality for treatment.

An all-German officiating team will take charge of the match. Daniel Schlager is the on-field referee and will be supported on the touchlines by assistant referees Sven Waschitzki and Tobias Fritsch. Robin Braun has been appointed as the fourth official. In the video operations room, Benjamin Cortus will serve as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), alongside Nicolas Winter as the Assistant VAR (AVAR).

Some updates have arrived from this morning’s training session, ahead of AC Milan’s clash against Olympiacos tomorrow.

There is no understating how substantial tomorrow’s game is for Milan. If they want to qualify for the Round of 16, they must win tomorrow, especially if they want to avoid an extra elimination round.

Of course, it will be difficult to do so, but history suggests that it’s not impossible to recover from their current position in Europe.

An update from training has arrived this morning, with PianetaMilan reporting that Tomori has indeed returned to training with the group at Milanello, as was hoped last night.

In fact, he has fully recovered and will be in contention for the game against Olympiacos tomorrow night, which is a major boost for Ruben Amorim, with Strahinja Pavlovic still absent.

In a recent development, however, Luka Modric may not be the only other player who’ll be missing tomorrow. Indeed, the report states that Francesco Camarda could also be absent.

Recent findings suggest that the young striker missed training today – as he’s suffering from some ankle pain – and his presence in tomorrow’s match is now in doubt. Considering Goncalo Ramos’ early substitution on Saturday, though, it may not be too much of a concern for Ruben Amorim, who seemingly wasn’t going to look to the youngster as a starter.

'Would be very difficult to stop' - Gary Lineker names the one thing Brighton need to become serious Premier League title challengers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City.
  • According to recent reports, brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City. A victory would have taken the high-flying Seagulls to within three points to leaders Arsenal.

According to recent reports, brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis. Their failure to convert chances proved costly, with Oli McBurnie stealing the game with a late brace.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Recent findings suggest that despite the result, Lineker was left hugely impressed by what he saw from the Seagulls. He described Brighton as the ‘best team to watch in the league’ when it comes to the quality of football.

The former Tottenham and Barcelona striker mentioned he believes the addition of a clinical centre-forward could make Albion a formidable proposition.

"If Brighton had a nine like Leicester had in Jamie Vardy, I think they would be serious title challengers," Lineker, 65, said.

"They create so many chances. They haven't got, or at least I've not seen, a real nine in there that sniffs out [goals].".

The former Match of the Day host acknowledged that the Seagulls had played some excellent football but could not find the finishing touch.

"I watched the Brighton game yesterday, and I still can't quite work out [how they didn’t score]," he stated.

"Well, I can, because they missed too many chances, and the opposition's keeper was unbelievable, but they played some incredibly good football.

"They couldn't score, which is unusual because they've scored more goals than any other team in the league this season.

"Even though they lost 2-0, I was thinking, God, Brighton are good.

"I go back to the point but if they had someone like a Vardy, wow, they'd be very difficult to stop, I think.".

Regardless, Lineker mentioned he ‘definitely can see’ Brighton in the Champions League next season.

According to recent reports, his fellow podcast pundit Micah Richards agreed with the assessment. But he also felt the result was particularly damaging to Brighton's ambitions.

The former Manchester City full-back suggested that, if the Seagulls were serious about making a push towards the top of the Premier League, winning at Hull was essential.

"I know it's ridiculous – and we're talking about jumping on the bandwagon and being reactionary – but I think for a real push, they had to win that game," he noted.

However, Richards, 38, was equally complimentary about the football Hürzeler's team are producing.

"I think they play some of the best football in the Premier League – they create so many chances," he remarked.

He agreed that they ideally need to sign a prolific number nine. But he was keen to stress that the comments were not intended as criticism of Albion’s current forwards – including Georginio Rutter, who started the match at Hull, and Charalampos Kostoulas.

"It's no disrespect to Rutter, he's just not got the clinical edge of a world-class player," Richards explained.

Richards also highlighted the contribution of midfielder Yasin Ayari, particularly his ability to make late runs into the penalty area.

Alan Shearer was another to praise Brighton's performance, describing the quality of their football and the pace at which they moved the ball.

"Great football, some brilliant football. They were passing and moving at pace – superb," the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer remarked.

The Newcastle legend added: "It was just one of those days where the keeper had his day and nothing was going to go past him. You have that and you just move on.”.

Shearer, 56, also felt the result should not overshadow the quality of Brighton's display.

"I think he [Hürzeler] will be disappointed with the result, but performance-wise, I thought they were brilliant,” he mentioned.

Brighton were not the only team to receive praise, with Richards also highlighting Bournemouth's recent formidable form.

The podcast trio agreed that the quality across the Premier League is improving, with Richards arguing that teams outside the traditional 'big six' are becoming increasingly difficult opponents.

In a recent development, for Brighton, however, Lineker's message was clear. He believes Hürzeler has a side capable of playing some of the best football in the country, but adding a striker with the instincts and finishing ability of Vardy could make them a much more dangerous proposition.
